- **A listed mega-cap establishing a repeatable non-dilutive-equity-financing rail for AI capex is a template.** If Alphabet, Amazon or Microsoft follows with the same structure, the market will have to underwrite hyperscaler capex as *perpetual* rather than *cyclical* —
- which compresses the multiple permanently. That is the structural read, and it is why yesterday's move was −7% on a company that beat on both lines.
- Note the 2-for-1 split is cosmetic; **the Class C is the news.** Watch META at the open — pre-market only −0.17%, so the initial damage may already be behind it.

- Brent at $113 is a reflationary one. They cannot both be right.
- The bond market's position is that oil's move is event-driven and supply-side — Houthi attacks and a *speculative* strike plan — and therefore not persistent into CPI.
- Yahoo's live blog framed it exactly that way:
- *"The bond market is calling oil's inflation bluff."* **The resolution test is XOM reporting this morning** (consensus EPS ~$3.71), which will say whether energy earnings confirm the spot move.
- **If crude holds above $100 with the 10Y sub-5%, the market is pricing oil as transitory and that is a fragile consensus —
- a single geopolitical de-escalation headline reverses both legs at once.** This also keeps yesterday's GM commodity-cost channel live:
- GM flagged input inflation approaching $2bn, and with Brent +50% since February that headwind is getting worse, not better.

- mega-cap AI capex announcements get sold (META −7%), hardware earnings that merely match get sold (LRCX −11.8%, IBM +11%→−5%), but **ordinary industrials and consumer names that reaffirm or nudge guidance above the high end get bid hard (POOL +14.4%, SPOT +11.1%)**.

**Macro calendar**

- **Yesterday:** no major US macro. The session was entirely Meta/Tesla-earnings digestion plus the yield move.
- Brent +4% on Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia and reports of planned post-midterm US/Israel strikes on Iran.
- **Today (Fri 10/23):** **08:30 ET initial jobless claims** (week ending Oct 17, ~225K est) —
- the fourth consecutive soft-ish labor/housing datapoint and the direct test of whether the sub-5% 10Y holds. **09:45 ET S&P Global flash PMIs** (manufacturing ~49.8 est) —
- **the single most important release of the week for this thesis**, because it dates the growth scare that the bond market just priced. **10:00 ET new home sales** (Sept).
- **15:00 ET Michigan consumer sentiment** (final Oct, ~68.9 est) and **leading indicators** revision. Kansas City Fed manufacturing at 11:00 ET.
- **Next week is the FOMC (28 Oct).** Markets have now priced out a hike almost entirely — **P(≥25bp) collapsed to ~10.5%** from markedly higher earlier in October.
- Consensus remains a hold. With the 10Y back below 5%, **the FOMC is no longer the week's dominant risk; the PMIs are.**
- **Rate path in one line:** the 10Y peaked at **5.3645% on Oct 7 (highest since April 2002)** and is now **4.953%** — a 41bp round-trip in eleven sessions.
- **Every long-duration equity multiple in the market is being marked off that number, not off earnings.**

**Earnings today**

- **Overnight (Thursday PM):** the consumer/housing complex reported well and was bid — **POOL +14.36%**, **SPOT +11.10%**, **KSS +11.82%**, **CNXC +13.77%**, **BMI +13.48%**, **ALLE +11.02%**, **R +10.49%**, **WCN +9.86%**, **ROP +9.73%**.
- Laggards on the prints: **OII −16.94%**, **GGG −15.32%**, **FCFS −14.75%**, **CRS −20.62%**.
- **Today is the lightest major-calendar day of a heavy week, with the FOMC looming.** **Before the open: AXP (American Express)** — the week's marquee name.
